name: The Bahamas
summary: The Bahamas has no forced heirship, but a surviving spouse of a person domiciled there can ask the court for reasonable provision. Trusts are well developed (Trustee Act, trust choice-of-law Act) and private foundations are available under the Foundations Act. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
family_claims: Part III of the Inheritance Act (Ch. 116) lets a surviving spouse seek a share if the will makes no reasonable financial provision; it applies only where the deceased was domiciled in The Bahamas. Section 24 gives conditional protection of the spouse's right to occupy the marital home.
foreign_law_note: Movables follow the testator's wishes and domicile law; real property follows Bahamian law. Under s. 7 of the Wills Act (Ch. 115) a testator domiciled abroad with Bahamian assets can make a will governed by Bahamian law. There is no statutory choice of nationality law.
trust_note: The Bahamas is not in the HCCH status table. Trustee Act, Ch. 176 (1998) and Trusts (Choice of Governing Law) Act, Ch. 170; heirship rights under foreign law are not recognised against a Bahamian trust. Private foundations: Foundations Act, Ch. 369D. No estate, inheritance or gift tax.
open_questions: Whether family provision extends beyond spouses (children, dependants) was not confirmed.
